title: Turkish Governor Fired After Posting Cycling Photos in Lycra; Petition Demands Reinstatement
excerpt: Mehmet Fatih Çiçekli, governor of Ardahan province, was dismissed by presidential decree after politicians accused him of abandoning the dignity of office by wearing cycling tights on social media. A petition with 10,000 signatures now demands his return.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ardahan Governor Mehmet Fatih Çiçekli was dismissed on July 17 for posting cycling photos in Lycra.
  • Politicians from AKP and CHP criticized him for undermining the dignity of his office.
  • A petition for his reinstatement has gathered 10,000 signatures, highlighting his contributions to youth sports.
  • Çiçekli defended his attire, emphasizing the importance of sports and being human over titles.
Dismissal Sparks Controversy
›Çiçekli dismissed on July 17 by presidential decree.
›Critics from both AKP and CHP condemned his cycling attire.
›Replaced by Ömer Hilmi Yamlı.
›No official reason provided for dismissal.

Mehmet Fatih Çiçekli, the governor of Turkey's northeastern Ardahan province, was dismissed from his post on July 17 after sharing social media images and videos of himself wearing Lycra cycling tights — a move that drew fierce criticism from politicians across party lines who accused him of undermining the dignity of public office.

The dismissal came via presidential decree signed by Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. No official reason was given. Çiçekli was replaced by Ömer Hilmi Yamlı.

Politicians Call Cycling Attire Unbecoming

The controversy erupted after images circulated on social media showing Çiçekli sporting black cycling tights and a red fitted top while riding his bicycle. Politicians from both the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) and the opposition Republican People's Party (CHP) took aim at his appearance.

"A governor in leggings? That simply won't do. Such governors should be removed from office — or at least issued a fig leaf."

— İnan Akgün Alp, CHP Member of Parliament

Alp also accused Çiçekli of "abandoning the seriousness and dignity of state office." Fellow critics had reprimanded him for "spending all day creating social media content" in recent months.

Şamil Tayyar, a deputy from Erdoğan's AKP, was equally blunt. "Neither citizens nor his own civil servants will take a governor in leggings seriously," Tayyar said. "He has no authority."

A Career Cut Short

Çiçekli entered Turkey's civil administration in 2004 and was appointed governor of Ardahan — a sparsely populated province near the Georgian border — in January 2026. He held the position for barely six months before his abrupt removal.

An avid cyclist, Çiçekli appeared to have used social media to promote an active lifestyle and sporting culture in the region. But his frequent posts in form-fitting athletic wear proved too much for Turkey's political establishment, where governors are traditionally expected to project a sober, formal image.

Petition Gathers 10,000 Signatures

The backlash against Çiçekli's dismissal has been swift. A petition demanding his reinstatement has already gathered 10,000 signatures, with supporters praising his work in the province.

"The decision to remove Ardahan Governor Mehmet Fatih Çiçekli from his post has caused sadness and concern among many citizens who care about the future of our province," the petition stated, adding that it "has no political aims."

Supporters noted that Çiçekli had "accomplished significant work" in sport and youth development during his brief tenure, crediting him with increasing sports activities for young people and developing a culture of participation.

Governor Defends Himself

Çiçekli has pushed back against his critics. "The clothes I'm wearing are sports clothes. I do sports in sports clothes," he said.

"Rather than living through titles and labels, it's good to know you're a human being and remain one. The things that make you yourself, such as sports, cycling and rowing, aren't bad things. They're things that everyone, at every age, should be doing."

— Mehmet Fatih Çiçekli, former Ardahan Governor

Broader Significance

The episode, unusual even by Turkish political standards, has drawn international attention for its blend of the absurd and the authoritarian. Turkey's system of presidential decrees gives Erdoğan broad powers to appoint and dismiss provincial governors at will, with no requirement to provide justification.

The case has also triggered a broader conversation about personal freedoms and official image in Turkey, where Erdoğan's government has increasingly policed public expression through social media regulations and legal pressure on dissent. Critics note the irony of cross-party agreement on removing a governor for cycling attire while the country grapples with far weightier governance challenges.

Support for Çiçekli Grows
›Petition for reinstatement has 10,000 signatures.
›Supporters praise his work in youth sports development.
›Petition claims no political aims.
›Citizens express sadness over his removal.
